transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-09
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Jordan (Atlas Procurement), Leila (Atlas Security), Tom (Atlas Legal), Anika (Platform)
---
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I know we had a stacked agenda here, so we'll try to run through the open MSA items, DPA exceptions, and then pricing and the procurement sign-off path. Ethan and I will cover the technical notes maybe halfway through.
[00:18] Jordan Kim: Thanks Maya, appreciate it. We have 4 folks here from Atlas: myself, Leila, Tom and Anika. We want to get clear on the gap list for risk and what the procurement committee needs to approve pricing. Also timeline — our board wants vendor acceptance by end of month.
[00:30] Tom Breuer: Hi — quick legal note, we still have the usual asks: liability cap language, indemnity carve-outs for certain regulated activity, and we flagged one section in section 9 — termination for convenience notice period. We'll walk through specifics.
[00:45] Leila Ortiz: From InfoSec, big items are SOC 2 Type II and the pen-test summary, plus KMS integration and whether keys can be customer-managed. Also data residency: can you guarantee European data stays in EU for EU tenant?
[01:05] Ethan Brooks: Yeah — hi all. For KMS we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations (we've done AWS KMS and Azure KeyVault). For private deployments / VPC we can also install with keys managed by the customer; for hosted we can offer envelope encryption and bring-your-own-key for certain plans. Draft note on that coming.
[01:30] Jordan Kim: Good. Pricing: we need committed tier pricing, burst pricing and overage calc spelled out. Procurement needs a one-pager that lays out per-token and embedding rates, plus discount steps tied to committed monthly spend.
[01:45] Maya Patel: Understood. We'll share a clean spreadsheet with committed tiers and burst rules. To manage expectations, the dedicated/reserved capacity tiers have different economics than hosted per-token. We'll call that out.
[02:05] Tom Breuer: On the MSA redlines we circulated — the big ask is to change the liability cap to a flat 12 months of fees vs. the 6 months currently. Also we're asking for explicit carve-outs for gross negligence and willful misconduct.
[02:30] Maya Patel: Right — we saw Tom's redline. Internally Redwood legal typically pushes for a 6 months fees cap except for exceptions; we can propose middle ground language: 12 months cap but with specific carve-outs limited in scope. I'll propose phrasing and rationale.
[02:55] Leila Ortiz: Another thing — audit logs and retention. We need logs preserved for 2 years for some of our regulated product lines. Do you have configurable retention windows?
[03:15] Ethan Brooks: We do. For dedicated and private, audit log retention is configurable; for hosted we have retention tiers and add-on long-term logs. We will note retention policies and export formats in the security doc we send.
[03:40] Jordan Kim: Okay — timeline: procurement review next Monday, legal approval by mid-October, and finance wants final pricing to publish. If we can get MSA settlement and SOC2 it's hopeful.
[03:55] Maya Patel: Sounds reasonable. Should we go item by item? Tom, can you call out the top 3 legal items so we can address them now.
[04:10] Tom Breuer: Sure. 1) Liability cap increase to 12 months fees; 2) Indemnity scope around third-party IP (we want broader protections); 3) Data breach notification timelines — request for 48 hours instead of 72.
[04:35] Maya Patel: For 48 hours, I know Redwood aims for 72 to complete triage, but we can discuss tightened SLA for initial notification — maybe 48 hours for initial notification and 72/7 for full impact analysis. I'll propose that compromise.
[04:55] Ethan Brooks: On IP indemnity — we can accept a limited indemnity for third-party claims where there is clear misuse. Need to scope out what constitutes misuse; we usually carve out customer content misuse.
[05:15] Leila Ortiz: Re: data residency, can you confirm if production inference for EU customers is processed in eu-west regions only, or can it fall back? We're worried about cross-border fallback.
[05:35] Ethan Brooks: For hosted we route to nearest region but customers can pin to EU-only model endpoints on the enterprise tier; dedicated and private obviously run in the customer VPC/region. We'll document routing and fallback policies — and note that for EU pinned endpoints we will not failover to non-EU without explicit authorization.
[05:55] Anika Shah: For our platform teams, we also need to understand network egress patterns — e.g., do calls go out to any third-party telemetry endpoints? That is a red flag for some of our compliance rules.
[06:15] Ethan Brooks: We do telemetry for health metrics but that can be routed via customer-managed collectors for private/dedicated; hosted has telemetry but we can provide options to disable or forward to customer endpoints in enterprise plans. We'll include a topology diagram.
[06:40] Jordan Kim: Great. On procurement process: do you have any standard vendor onboarding packet we can slot into our procurement portal? We typically need W9, ins cert, MSA v1, DPA, evidence of SOC2.
[06:55] Maya Patel: Yes — we'll provide a vendor onboarding bundle: W9, insurance cert (we'll generate), the current MSA and DPA redlines, SOC 2 summary, and a short compliance pack.
[07:10] Tom Breuer: Insurance minimums — Atlas requires $5M general liability and cyber extortion coverage. Can you confirm?
[07:25] Maya Patel: Redwood's standard includes $5M general liability and $3M cyber; I will check if we can extend cyber to $5M and get back to you. I'll mark as action item.
[07:40] Leila Ortiz: Regarding the DPA, we have a list of data subprocessors we need disclosed. Do you publish a subprocessor list?
[07:52] Maya Patel: We do maintain a subprocessor registry and we'll share the current list; for private deployments the customer can choose to control subprocessors entirely.
[08:05] Jordan Kim: Good. Pricing question again: if we sign a 12-month committed reserved capacity contract, what happens with auto-scaling bursts beyond the committed capacity — how are those billed?
[08:20] Ethan Brooks: Bursts above committed capacity are billed at a higher per-token or per-instance rate depending on the plan; we'll define burst multipliers in the pricing sheet. For Dedicated we can provision overflow pools or temporarily spin up host capacity under an agreed burst rate.
[08:40] Jordan Kim: Procurement needs the exact formula — % of committed, multiplier steps. Can you show an example clause?
[08:55] Maya Patel: Yes, we'll include example scenarios: 20% burst for up to 4 hours/day at 1.5x, 100% burst at 2x beyond that, etc. We'll make the spreadsheet clear with formulas.
[09:10] Tom Breuer: Back to MSA — termination for convenience: we prefer a 60 days notice but would accept 30 if there are pro-rated refunds for unused committed capacity.
[09:25] Maya Patel: Our standard is 30-day notice, but for reserved capacity contracts we often negotiate pro-rated refunds or early termination fees. We'll propose a pro-rata refund schedule to balance risk.
[09:40] Leila Ortiz: Also confirm SSO/SAML and SCIM support for user provisioning.
[09:52] Ethan Brooks: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning across enterprise plans. We'll include SSO docs and an implementation guide.
[10:05] Jordan Kim: Onboard timing: if legal signs off by Oct 16, procurement needs 5 business days to route to finance — we're targeting Oct 24 as hard no-later date to get services live in November.
[10:25] Maya Patel: Noted. We'll coordinate to hit Oct 16 legal signoff.
[10:35] [pause sounds, some cross-talk]
[11:00] Ethan Brooks: Quick technical flag — for Atlas's PII-heavy flows, we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment. Hosted can be configured but there are more controls on dedicated for KV cache isolation and guaranteed CPU/GPU residency.
[11:22] Anika Shah: For testing we plan a short POC: 2 weeks of inference at low volume to validate latency, and a data handling audit. Who owns the POC SOW?
[11:35] Maya Patel: Redwood can issue an SOW for a POC — we'll include success criteria, sample load profile, and what data will be used (we recommend synthetic data where possible). We'll send draft SOW.
[11:52] Tom Breuer: When you say 'synthetic' — we need to ensure the PII redaction step is spelled out. We may provide tokenized test data.
[12:05] Ethan Brooks: Understood. We'll document the recommended redaction and tokenization process.
[12:15] Jordan Kim: One last procurement check — can you accept our preferred payment terms (Net45) or do you require Net30? Finance flagged Net45 as their default.
[12:30] Maya Patel: Redwood standard is Net30, but for enterprise we can consider Net45 with a small early-pay discount or slight price adjustment. We'll surface that to our finance team.
[12:45] Leila Ortiz: Re: SLA — Atlas expects 99.95% for inference endpoints and 99.9% for control plane APIs. Are those in line with your dedicated offering?
[13:05] Ethan Brooks: Dedicated can be configured to 99.95% target; hosted typical is 99.9% for control plane; we'll quote exact SLOs and credit formulas in the SLA addendum. Note that per-region outages and force majeure carveouts apply.
[13:30] Tom Breuer: Also add a scheduled maintenance window max of X hours/month? Our procurement wants limits so we can schedule around it.
[13:45] Maya Patel: We'll propose an SLA addendum with scheduled maintenance windows communicated 30 days in advance and an annual max; I'll get exact numbers from ops.
[13:58] Jordan Kim: Ok — maybe we pivot to the specific MSA clause language — Maya, do you have a proposed compromise written?
[14:10] Maya Patel: Yes. High level: propose 12-month liability cap, carve-outs for gross negligence and willful misconduct, initial breach notice within 48 hours, full report within 7 days, pro-rated refunds on early term for reserved capacity, KMS BYOK for enterprise, and subprocessor registry shared. We'll send a redline packet that shows current MSA with proposed language.
[14:40] Tom Breuer: Do you accept customer-specific audit rights under NDA for certain on-prem/pivotal deployments? We need to be able to audit logs on occasion.
[14:55] Ethan Brooks: For private we can grant audit rights; for hosted we usually provide audit artifacts and an annual attestation. We can scope customer-specific audits via a separate SOC or on-prem kit — depends on plan.
[15:15] Leila Ortiz: Any blockers on our end for security sign-off? We need the SOC2 report and KMS plan, and the subprocessor list.
[15:30] Maya Patel: We'll share SOC2 Type II and a technical appendix on key management this week.
[15:40] Jordan Kim: Perfect. Can we move to next steps recap?
[15:50] Maya Patel: Sure. Recap: Redwood to send redline MSA summary and proposed cap language (Maya), SOC2 and pen-test notes plus subprocessor list (Maya), technical note on VPC/private topology and BYOK (Ethan), pricing spreadsheet with committed tiers and burst rules and Net45 options (Maya), and draft POC SOW (Maya/Ethan). Atlas to return a prioritized list of remaining DPA exceptions and insurance confirmation (Tom/Jordan).
[16:25] Tom Breuer: We'll record those and aim to get legal comments back by Oct 16.
[16:35] Jordan Kim: Procurement will need the pricing spreadsheet by Oct 10 to route for approvals. Finance sign-off by Oct 24 is our target.
[16:45] Maya Patel: We'll prioritize getting the pricing spreadsheet and SOC2 artifacts by Oct 10.
[16:55] Leila Ortiz: One small thing — can we have a single point of contact for security questions during the POC?
[17:05] Ethan Brooks: Yes, that'll be me. I'll be the technical POC.
[17:15] Maya Patel: I'll send calendar invites for the follow-up risk meeting and upload docs to the secure share. Any other open items?
[17:30] Jordan Kim: None from procurement. Thanks everyone.
[17:40] Maya Patel: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the deliverables and schedule.
[17:50] [call ends]
---
